response.task_summary: Predict whether a household/person receives food stamps in ACS data, emphasizing stable socioeconomic and household-structure signals over domain-specific shortcuts.

ranking.rationale: Age is a core, stable driver of SNAP eligibility and household need across domains.
Education strongly tracks long-run economic opportunity and tends to generalize well.
Number of workers in the family is a direct, portable proxy for household resources.
Weeks worked captures labor-market attachment and income stability.
Usual weekly hours worked is a strong, semantically meaningful income proxy.
Recent work status is highly predictive of current earnings and assistance need.
Marital status affects household composition and economic resources in a fairly stable way.
Presence and age of children is directly relevant to household need and benefit eligibility.
Relationship to reference person helps infer household structure and dependency burden.
Sex can correlate with labor supply and household composition, though it is a weaker proxy.
Disability status is a meaningful and stable predictor of economic hardship.
Public coverage reflects low-income status, but may be partly downstream and policy-linked.
Citizenship status can matter for eligibility and access, but is a sensitive demographic proxy.
Nativity may correlate with eligibility and socioeconomic status, but is not a direct need signal.
Race can capture structural inequality, but is a sensitive shortcut and less causally direct.
State can reflect policy variation and local conditions, but is a domain identifier and brittle.
Survey year may absorb temporal drift, but it is a strong domain marker rather than a stable cause.
Layoff status is informative about short-term hardship, though noisy and transient.
Looking for work indicates unemployment, but can be unstable and context-dependent.
Recent childbirth can affect household expenses, but it is a narrow and low-frequency signal.
Hearing difficulty is a disability-related proxy, but weaker than the direct disability indicator.
Vision difficulty is similarly relevant but usually secondary to broader disability status.
Cognitive difficulty matters for hardship, but overlaps with the more general disability feature.
Military service is only indirectly related to food assistance need and can be cohort-specific.
Ancestry is largely a demographic artifact with weak direct relevance to SNAP receipt.
Place of birth is mostly a demographic descriptor and can act as a brittle shortcut.
Occupation is often highly predictive but can overfit to local labor-market composition and coding.
English-speaking ability is a sensitive proxy that may spuriously encode nativity and ethnicity rather than stable need.
